title: Operation Fort: Polish forced-labour ring in the West Midlands (UK)
summary: Operation Fort, led by West Midlands Police with National Crime Agency support, is described by the UK government as the largest case prosecuted under UK modern slavery legislation. Vulnerable Polish nationals, including homeless people, former prisoners and people with alcohol dependency, were lured to England with offers of work, free or subsidised accommodation, food and travel, then put to work on farms, in recycling centres, poultry factories and parcel warehouses while wages were paid into gang-controlled bank accounts; some received as little as £10 a week. Police estimated up to 400 people were exploited and the gang earned more than £2 million. Bank cards and identity documents were confiscated and threats and violence used to stop people leaving. On 5 July 2019 Birmingham Crown Court sentenced Ignacy Brzezinski to 11 years, Wojciech Nowakowski to six and a half years and Jan Sadowski to three years, following convictions of five others in an earlier trial.
